newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products-USG gasolines reverse, end down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products-USG gasolines reverse, end down.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast conventional gasoline differentials dove sharply by late Wednesday, paring the early session strength to finish slightly lower on the day
Midcontinent gasoline differentials slid lower on profit taking, eating away at gains seen in recent days.
On the NYMEX, June gasoline jumped 1.14 cents to settle at 66.53 cents a gallon while June heating oil dipped 0.09 cent to finish at 57.55 cents a gallon.
- U.S. GULF COAST

Active refinery buying in the conventional M1 gasoline evaporated shortly after midday, forcing sellers to chase bids to between 2.75 to 2.90 cents under the June NYMEX by late day, traders said. Those barrels changed hands as high as 1.50 cents under the June NYMEX early in the afternoon.

Refiners emerged as heavy buyers ahead of Tuesday evening's scheduling deadline, driving differentials about 2.00 cents up. Those barrels were talked even with the June NYMEX Wednesday on an upline basis of the Colonial Pipeline, traders said.

However, many refiners appeared to simply roll their short positions forward, and with the next scheduling deadline for the conventional M1 gasoline coming up Friday evening, some players said another bullish spike may be on its way.
"Refiners are out for now ... but it's only a respite," one Gulf trader said.
"It could go either way, but the odds are that gasoline will pop up, but heating oil's probably going to head lower," another player commented.
Prompt heating oil differentials were talked between 2.30 and 2.40 cents under the June NYMEX.
- U.S. MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent levels weakened in the afternoon amid profit taking before the long holiday weekend. Prices were also pressured down by talk that 14th cycle barrels on the Explorer pipeline will begin to arrive late May -- ahead of earlier expectations that the barrels would all arrive in June because of continued delays on the system, players said.
Explorer officials were not immediately available for comment.
Group Three prompt unleaded differentials slid 1.50 cents Wednesday, with deals at 5.00 and 5.75 cents over the screen done for Friday delivery.
"Most everyone got their requirements covered last week," said one products trader, noting last week's run-up in prompt barrels due to demand.
The Chicago markets were also lower, with prompt unleaded down by 0.75 cent to 1.75/2.00 cents over the screen. Any barrels were pegged on par.
- NEW YORK HARBOR
The Harbor took a backseat to the Gulf Wednesday as differentials showed little movement, according to traders.
Prompt low sulphur diesel barrels changed hands at 0.40 cents over the June NYMEX, down about 0.20 cent from levels talked Tuesday, players said.
However, gasoline trade was thin in the region, with buyers reluctant to commit to deals.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
